Neoantigen-specific T cells from the peripheral blood can migrate into an intracranial glioblastoma tumour. The vaccine has the potential to favourably alter the immune milieu of glioblastoma. [Ref6212:Keskin et al., 2019]

c_vaccine_name: Personal neoantigen cancer vaccine
c_description: Neoantigen-based cancer vaccines are designed to target the unique immunogenic mutations arising in each patient's tumor. Peptide binding to MHC is a critical gateway to both the initiation of a T-cell immune response by the antigen presenting cell (APC), and to the detection and elimination of tumor cells presenting the particular peptide by the stimulated cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL). The attraction of neoantigens as cancer targets for the immune system results from the structural and geographical features of the mutation. Neoantigen peptides are only found in tumor cells, so CTLs should show exquisite specificity, reducing the opportunity for autoimmune disease. [Ref6214:Fritsch et al., 2014]

c_vaccine_name: Whole tumor cell-based leukemia vaccine
c_description: Whole tumor cell-based vaccines administered within the first 2 to 3 months after allogeneic stem cell transplantation may enhance graft-vs.-leukemia responses. Irradiated autologous cancer cells provide a source of tumor antigens at the vaccination site. Granulocyte macrophage colony-stimulating factor (GM-CSF) secreted by irradiated bystander cells stimulates the recruitment, maturation and immunostimulatory activity of dendritic cells (DCs) at the vaccination site. Autologous whole tumor cell-based vaccination may tip the balance between leukemia-specific and alloreactive T cell responses in favor of a graft-vs.-leukemia (GvL) effect. [Ref6215:Burkhardt and Wu, 2013]

c_vaccine_name: Adenovirus-vectored therapeutic vaccine (Ad-Ii-E1E2E6E7)

This immunodominance suppressed T cell responses to the KRAS neoantigens, reducing SLATEv1â€™s efficacy in targeting KRAS-mutant tumors. Epitopes competing for the same HLA molecule led to differences in immunogenicity: KRAS G12V and G12D were less immunogenic when co-delivered with TP53 S127Y on the same vaccine cassette. 42% (8/19 patients) achieved stable disease. Progression-free survival was 1.9 months (median), while overall survival was 7.9 months (median). A molecular response (â‰¥30% reduction in circulating tumor DNA levels) was observed in 33% of evaluable patients (4/12). c_vaccine_name: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) vaccine
c_description: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) vaccine is for Burkitt lymphoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, non-Hodgkin lymphoma, posttransplant lymphoproliferative disease (PTLD) (B cell malignancies), nasopharyngeal carcinoma, gastric carcinoma (epithelial cell malignancies). Gp42 is a glycoprotein on the surface of EBV that plays a crucial role in the virusâ€™s ability to infect host cells, particularly by interacting with HLA class II molecules on B cells. There are 2 vulnerable sites on gp42 protein: receptor-binding  (blocked by A10 and F-2-1) and hydrophobic pocket (blocked by 4C12) regions. A10 and F-2-1 bind to overlapping epitopes on gp42. They both block gp42â€™s interaction with HLA class II, preventing EBV binding to B cells. A10 is more potent than F-2-1 due to higher binding affinity and broader coverage of the epitope. Hydrophobic pocket region is critical for cell membrane fusion activation. 4C12 targets the hydrophobic pocket of gp42, disrupting fusion without blocking receptor binding. It represents a novel mechanism of action, as it does not interfere with the HLA class II interaction.  [Ref6284:Bu et al., 2024]

c_vaccine_name: MUC1 12-mer–STn(T3)–OVA₃₂₃₋₃₃₉ Glycopeptide Conjugate Vaccine

The MUC1 component contains the immunodominant PDTRP motif and is glycosylated with sialyl-Tn antigen at threonine 3. The vaccine is designed to induce highly specific humoral immune response against tumor-associated glycopeptide structures. A triethylene glycol spacer connects the antigen to the T-helper epitope, which provides co-stimulatory signals for B-cell activation. Vaccination of DO11.10 transgenic mice resulted in production of anti-MUC1-STn IgG antibodies with immunological memory (1/3 mice responsive). Antibodies showed exceptional specificity, requiring both correct peptide sequence and STn glycan for recognition; neutralization assays (1:4000-1:16000 dilutions) demonstrated nearly complete neutralization by the complete MUC1-STn glycopeptide epitope only, with no cross-reactivity to unglycosylated MUC1, STn on different peptide backbones (MUC4), or unglycosylated controls. MUC1 is a membrane-bound glycoprotein overexpressed in aberrant or deglycosylated forms in various epithelial cancers including breast, prostate, ovarian, gastric, and colon carcinomas [Ref6788:Dziadek et al., 2005].

c_vaccine_name: MF59/CpG ODN1826-adjuvanted MUC1-Maltose Binding Protein (MBP) Vaccine
c_description: A recombinant fusion protein vaccine containing MUC1 tumor antigen (seven tandem repeats, 7×VNTR) fused to maltose binding protein (MBP), adjuvanted with MF59 oil-in-water emulsion and CpG ODN1826. Vaccination stimulates MUC1-specific humoral and cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL) responses against tumor cells expressing the MUC1 antigen. MF59 prolongs local retention of CpG 1826 and antigen in lymph nodes (>24h), enhances DC maturation by downregulating IL-6/STAT3, and promotes Th1 polarization. In preclinical studies, demonstrated significant tumor inhibition in B16-MUC1 melanoma with 80% survival at 70 days (prophylactic) and 60% at 50 days (therapeutic) vs. 30% with CpG alone. MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein expressed by most glandular and ductal epithelial cells, is overexpressed in various cancers including breast, prostate, and melanoma [Ref6789:Jie et al., 2022].

c_vaccine_name: MUC1 mRNA/CTLA-4 siRNA Co-Delivery Mannose-Modified NLE Vaccine

The hybrid platform (90% exosomal membrane, 10% synthetic lipids) targets dendritic cells via mannose receptors, enabling in situ MUC1 antigen expression and simultaneous CTLA-4 checkpoint silencing. MUC1, a tumor-associated mucin overexpressed and aberrantly glycosylated in TNBC, contains multiple CTL epitopes in its VNTR domain. In 4T1 mouse models, vaccination significantly enhanced CD8+ T cell infiltration, IFN-γ production, and MUC1-specific cytotoxicity compared to monotherapies (p < 0.01), demonstrating synergistic antitumor immunity with favorable safety profile [Ref6790:Monfaredan et al., 2025].

c_vaccine_name: MUC1-MALP2 (Pam₂Cys) Conjugate Vaccines (unglycosylated/Tn/T)
c_description: A synthetic self-adjuvanting glycopeptide vaccine comprising MUC1 VNTR glycopeptide antigens covalently conjugated to macrophage activating lipopeptide 2 (MALP2) adjuvant via a triethyleneglycol spacer. Three variants were evaluated: unglycosylated, Tn-perglycosylated (GalNAc-α-Ser/Thr), and T-perglycosylated (Gal(β1-3)GalNAc-α-Ser/Thr) at five sites within the MUC1 VNTR. The MALP2 component (MALP2 peptide-Pam2CysGly) acts as a TLR2/6 agonist enabling direct B-cell activation. Vaccination of C57BL/6 mice induced high-titer class-switched IgG antibodies (IgG1, IgG2b, IgG3) without external adjuvants or helper T-cell epitopes, demonstrating T-cell-independent class switching. The unglycosylated variant exhibited highest antibody titres. Antibodies recognized MUC1 VNTR epitopes including SAPDTRPAP, with Tn-glycosylated variant showing cross-reactivity to unglycosylated and T-glycosylated forms. No cytotoxic T-cell responses were observed. Induced IgG antibodies are potentially capable of mediating ADCC and complement activation, though not functionally tested [Ref6791:McDonald et al., 2014].

c_vaccine_name: MUC1 ΔTM-HSP70 Chimeric DNA Vaccine
c_description: A chimeric DNA vaccine encoding a fusion protein of transmembrane- and C-terminal domain-deleted Mucin 1 (Muc1 ΔTM) and heat shock protein 70 (HSP70), with potential antineoplastic activity. The construct includes a tyrosinase leader sequence to direct secretion of the fusion protein from transfected cells. Upon intramuscular administration of the plasmid DNA, muscle cells express and secrete the Muc1-HSP70 fusion protein, which is captured by antigen-presenting cells (APCs) via HSP70 receptor-mediated interaction. This facilitates MHC Class I cross-presentation and delivers maturation signals to APCs, enhancing the priming of Muc1-specific CD8+ cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL) responses. HSP70 serves as a built-in molecular adjuvant. Vaccination induces robust Muc1-specific cellular immune responses, including CD8+ T-cell proliferation (65.5% vs. 41.8% for ΔTM alone), significantly increased IFN-γ-secreting T cells (P<0.01), and potent cytotoxic activity against Muc1-expressing tumor cells. In preventive models, 4 of 7 vaccinated mice remained tumor-free following B16/Muc1 challenge (P<0.01). The vaccine also demonstrated therapeutic efficacy, significantly reducing tumor volumes in established B16/Muc1 melanoma in C57BL/6 mice (P<0.05) [Ref6792:Choi et al., 2011].

c_vaccine_name: H1 / CAF01
c_adjuvant: The adjuvant is CAF01. Composed of cationic liposomes (DDA) and trehalose-6,6-dibehenate (TDB) [Ref6795:Klessing et al., 2020].
c_preparation: The H1 tuberculosis subunit vaccine was prepared by formulating a recombinant fusion protein consisting of Ag85B and ESAT-6 with the liposomal adjuvant CAF01. Prior to immunization, the H1 antigen was allowed to adsorb to the CAF01 adjuvant for 60 minutes on ice before subcutaneous injection [Ref6795:Klessing et al., 2020].
c_antigen: H1 fusion protein composed of Ag85B and ESAT-6 from Mycobacterium tuberculosis [Ref6795:Klessing et al., 2020].

c_vaccine_name: ARM
c_adjuvant: The adjuvant is CpG oligodeoxynucleotide 1826 (CpG ODN 1826) [Ref6796:Hu et al., 2025].
c_preparation: The ARM fusion protein was recombinantly expressed and purified, then dissolved in phosphate-buffered saline (PBS) and mixed with CpG ODN 1826 prior to intramuscular immunization [Ref6796:Hu et al., 2025].
c_antigen: ARM fusion protein composed of Ag85B, Rv2660c, and MPT70 from Mycobacterium tuberculosis [Ref6796:Hu et al., 2025].

c_vaccine_name: H4-IC31
c_adjuvant: IC31 vaccine adjuvant consists of the antibacterial peptide KLK and oligodeoxynucleotide ODN1a (TLR9 agonist) [Ref6798:Rozot et al., 2020].
c_preparation:
The vaccine is prepared by formulating the recombinant H4 fusion protein (Ag85B–TB10.4) with the IC31 adjuvant.
Each dose contained 15 μg of H4 protein combined with 500 nmol of IC31 and was administered under controlled clinical trial conditions [Ref6798:Rozot et al., 2020].
c_antigen: H4 fusion protein composed of Ag85B and TB10.4 from Mycobacterium tuberculosis [Ref6798:Rozot et al., 2020].

c_vaccine_name: AHB-SeNPs
c_adjuvant: The adjuvant is Selenium nanoparticles (SeNPs) [Ref6799:Ge et al., 2024].
c_antigen: AHB fusion protein composed of Ag85A, HspX, and bovine neutrophil β-defensin-5 (B5).
c_preservative: Selenium nanoparticles were synthesized by reducing sodium selenite with ascorbic acid, using polyvinyl pyrrolidone (PVP K30) as a stabilizer.The AHB fusion protein was expressed in E. coli, purified, and endotoxin was removed. The vaccine was prepared by mixing AHB protein with SeNPs in PBS prior to intranasal administration [Ref6799:Ge et al., 2024].

c_vaccine_name: AH-PB
c_adjuvant: The adjuvant is Poly I:C (polyinosinic–polycytidylic acid) [Ref6800:Liang et al., 2022].
c_preparation: Fusion genes (Ag85A–HspX) were cloned, expressed recombinantly, and purified. Proteins were formulated with Poly I:C (± β-defensin-5) [Ref6800:Liang et al., 2022].
c_antigen: AH fusion proteins genetically linking Ag85A (FbpA) and HspX [Ref6800:Liang et al., 2022].

c_vaccine_name: Tetravalent MUC1-STn Glycopeptide-Pam₃CSK₄ Vaccine
c_description: A fully synthetic self-adjuvanting tetravalent vaccine containing four copies of MUC1 tandem repeat (VNTR) glycopeptide antigens bearing sialyl-Tn (STn) tumor-associated carbohydrate antigens at position S15, covalently conjugated to the TLR2 agonist lipopeptide Pam₃CSK₄ through click chemistry. Immunization of mice elicited predominantly IgG2a antibodies (IgG2a/IgG1 ratio >2.0), indicating a Th1-biased immune response. The antisera demonstrated strong binding to MCF-7 breast cancer cells and induced >90% tumor cell death through complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC) via the alternative pathway. The tetravalent presentation showed a significant cluster effect: compared to monovalent and divalent versions, it enhanced tumor cell recognition and cytotoxic activity despite lower antibody titers, with divalent vaccines producing highest titers but weaker binding [Ref6794:Cai et al., 2014].

c_vaccine_name: MUC1-PADRE-Pam₃CysSer Tricomponent Vaccines (unglycosylated/Tn/T)
c_description: A fully synthetic self-adjuvanting tricomponent vaccine consisting of the 20-amino acid MUC1 VNTR domain covalently conjugated to the universal T-cell helper peptide PADRE and the lipopeptide immunoadjuvant Pam₃CysSer. Three variants were prepared: unglycosylated (vaccine 1), bearing five Tn antigens (vaccine 2), or five T antigens (vaccine 3). The vaccines spontaneously self-assemble into nanoparticles (17-25 nm) in aqueous solution. Vaccination elicited robust antibody responses without external adjuvants, with IgG titers of 1775-8400; unglycosylated (8,400) > Tn (≈3,000) > T (≈1,775). Antibodies showed no cross-reactivity between variants. The response was Th2-skewed (IgG1 > IgG2c) with high IgG3 levels (1,000-4,000), suggesting multivalent presentation effects. Sera antibodies bound to MCF7 breast cancer cells and B16.MUC1 melanoma cells. Pam₃CysSer acts as a TLR1-TLR2 agonist providing self-adjuvanting activity. MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein, is overexpressed in an aberrant or deglycosylated form in over 90% of solid tumors including cancers of the breast, prostate, pancreas, and ovary [Ref6793:Wilkinson et al., 2012].

c_vaccine_name: Plant-expressed Hyp-Ara₃-glycosylated LTB-MUC1-6His Vaccine
c_description: A peptide vaccine containing the MUC1 tumor-associated tandem repeat peptide fused to heat-labile enterotoxin B subunit (LTB), produced in Nicotiana benthamiana plants using the magnICON™ viral expression system. The MUC1 peptide undergoes plant-specific O-linked hydroxyproline arabinosylation with tri-arabinan, essential for immune recognition and antigenicity. Vaccination of MUC1 transgenic mice with LTB-MUC1-6His plus CpG ODN adjuvant successfully broke self-antigen tolerance, inducing anti-MUC1 IgG, IgG1, and IgG2a antibody responses with significantly higher titers compared to controls (P < 0.05). CpG ODN shifted the immune response from Th2 bias toward Th1. This is the first plant-derived breast cancer antigen to demonstrate breach of tolerance in a transgenic mouse model. LTB serves as a carrier protein with mucosal-targeting and immunomodulatory properties. MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein expressed by most glandular and ductal epithelial cells, is overexpressed and aberrantly glycosylated in various cancers including breast, prostate, and ovarian cancers [Ref6801:Pinkhasov et al., 2011].

c_vaccine_name: pcDNA3-hMUC1 DNA Vaccine
c_description: A plasmid DNA vaccine encoding human tumor-associated epithelial mucin 1 (MUC1). The human MUC1 gene (GenBank accession J05582) is cloned into the pcDNA3 mammalian expression vector for intramuscular delivery. Vaccination with pcDNA3-hMUC1 induced potent cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL) responses with a 30-fold increase in CD8+ IFN-γ-producing T-cells compared to control (p<0.005). The vaccine generated a Th1-type immune response characterized by elevated IFN-γ production (2.7 vs 1.6 ng/mL, p<0.001) with no increase in IL-10 or CD4+ IFN-γ+ cells. In a preclinical colon cancer mouse model (CT26/hMUC1 cells), pcDNA3-hMUC1 immunization demonstrated significant tumor growth inhibition sustained up to 25 days post-challenge with reduced tumor weights (p<0.005). MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein with immunogenic 20-amino acid tandem repeat sequences, is overexpressed in an incompletely glycosylated form in various human cancers, exposing immunogenic epitopes that evoke immune responses against cancer cells [Ref6802:Jeon et al., 2007].

c_vaccine_name: pMUC1/pmuIL-18 DNA Vaccine
c_description: A bivalent plasmid DNA vaccine consisting of two co-administered plasmids encoding human MUC1 antigen (pMUC1) and murine interleukin-18 adjuvant (pmuIL-18). The pMUC1 plasmid encodes a 508 amino acid human MUC1 protein containing a truncated tandem repeat domain with 6.5 repeats. The two plasmids must be mixed together prior to intradermal injection for therapeutic efficacy; administration of either plasmid alone or at separate sites provides no protection. Vaccination in MUC1 transgenic mice breaks tolerance to MUC1 and induces significant tumor protection (70% tumor-free vs. 0% with single agents, P=0.003) and prolonged survival (>90 days) after subcutaneous challenge with MC38/MUC1 colorectal adenocarcinoma cells. Protection is mediated primarily by CD4+ T cells with contributions from CD8+ T cells. The vaccine induces durable memory responses with 82% of mice protected upon tumor rechallenge 8 weeks later, and promotes epitope spreading with 71% protection against MUC1-negative MC38 tumors. MUC1, a transmembrane glycoprotein normally expressed on ductal epithelia, is overexpressed in hypoglycosylated forms in adenocarcinomas of the breast, prostate, lung, colon, ovary, and pancreas [Ref6803:Snyder et al., 2006].

c_vaccine_name: DNA vaccine encoding BAB1_0263 and BAB1_0278 open reading frames of Brucella abortus
A986 + MPL/QS21
c_description: A986 + MPL/QS21 is a multistage recombinant fusion protein tuberculosis vaccine composed of Ag85A, Rv2028c, Rv2029c, and Rv3126c, formulated with MPL/QS21 adjuvant and administered as a booster following BCG priming to enhance protective immunity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis [Ref6807:Chen et al., 2024].
c_adjuvant: MPL/QS21 is used as the adjuvant [Ref6807:Chen et al., 2024].
c_preparation: The A986 fusion protein was recombinantly expressed and purified, then formulated with the MPL/QS21 adjuvant prior to subcutaneous administration as a booster vaccine following BCG priming [Ref6807:Chen et al., 2024].
c_antigen: A986 is a recombinant multistage fusion protein composed of Ag85A, Rv2028c, Rv2029c, and Rv3126c [Ref6807:Chen et al., 2024].

c_vaccine_name: AER in PLGA nanoparticles + CpG + MPLA
c_adjuvant: The vaccine includes CpG (a TLR9 agonist) and MPLA (a TLR4 agonist) as immunostimulatory adjuvants [Ref6808:Szachniewicz et al., 2024].
c_preparation: The recombinant AER fusion protein was encapsulated within PLGA (poly(D,L-lactic-co-glycolic acid)) nanoparticles together with CpG and MPLA. Each dose contained 8 μg AER, 2.5 μg CpG, and 1 μg MPLA, incorporated into approximately 400 μg PLGA nanoparticles prior to subcutaneous administration [Ref6808:Szachniewicz et al., 2024].
c_antigen: AER is a recombinant fusion protein composed of Ag85B, ESAT-6, and Rv2034 antigens of Mycobacterium tuberculosis [Ref6808:Szachniewicz et al., 2024].

c_adjuvant: The vaccine is formulated with CAF®01, a cationic liposome adjuvant consisting of DDA and TDB [Ref6809:Woodworth et al., 2021].
c_preparation: The H107 antigen was produced as a recombinant multi-antigen fusion protein and formulated with the CAF®01 adjuvant, a cationic liposome system composed of DDA and TDB, prior to subcutaneous administration [Ref6809:Woodworth et al., 2021].
c_antigen: H107 is a recombinant fusion protein composed of eight Mycobacterium tuberculosis antigens, including PPE68, ESAT-6 (four repeats), EspI, EspC, EspA, MPT64, MPT70, and MPT83 [Ref6809:Woodworth et al., 2021].

c_vaccine_name: GamTBvac
c_description: GamTBvac is a recombinant fusion protein tuberculosis vaccine containing Ag85A, ESAT-6, and CFP10, formulated with CpG and a dextran-based adjuvant system, and designed as a BCG booster [Ref6810:Tkachuk et al., 2020].
c_adjuvant: Adjuvant containing dextran 500 kDa, diethylaminoethyl (DEAE)-dextran 500 kDa, and CpG oligodeoxynucleotides (ODN) [Ref6810:Tkachuk et al., 2020].
c_preparation: GamTBvac is made of two combined (fusion) tuberculosis proteins mixed with a dextran-based adjuvant and CpG to help stimulate the immune system, and it is prepared as a liquid injection given under the skin [Ref347:Verreck et al., 2001].
c_antigen: GamTBvac contains ESAT6, CFP10, and Ag85A Mycobacterium tuberculosis [Ref6810:Tkachuk et al., 2020]

c_vaccine_name: ERA005f
c_description: ERA005f is a multistage recombinant fusion protein tuberculosis vaccine formulated with alum that induces strong Th1 and Th17 immune responses and inhibits Mycobacterium tuberculosis growth in a mouse model [Ref6811:Fan et al., 2023].
c_adjuvant: The vaccine was formulated with alum [Ref6811:Fan et al., 2023].
c_preparation: The ERA005f fusion protein was expressed in E. coli, purified using nickel affinity and ion-exchange chromatography, refolded, and then mixed with alum adjuvant [Ref6811:Fan et al., 2023].
c_antigen: ERA005f is a fusion protein composed of ESAT-6 (Rv3875), Rv2628, and Ag85B (Rv1886c) M. tuberculosis antigens [Ref6811:Fan et al., 2023].

c_adjuvant: The adjuvant is IC31 [Ref6812:Tait et al., 2024].
c_antigen: H56 is a recombinant fusion protein composed of Ag85B, ESAT-6 and Rv2660c [Ref6812:Tait et al., 2024].
c_preservative: H56 is a recombinant fusion protein composed of Ag85B, ESAT-6, and Rv2660c that was manufactured under GMP conditions and formulated with the IC31 adjuvant, which consists of a synthetic cationic peptide (KLK) and an immunostimulatory oligodeoxynucleotide (ODN1a), prior to intramuscular administration [Ref6812:Tait et al., 2024].

c_vaccine_name: Spore-FP1
c_adjuvant: The adjuvant is PolyI:C [Ref6813:White et al., 2023].
c_preparation: The FP1 fusion protein is adsorbed onto heat-inactivated Bacillus subtilis spores and formulated with PolyI:C in sterile saline [Ref6813:White et al., 2023].
c_antigen: The antigen is a fusion protein composed of Ag85B, Acr (HspX) and HBHA heparin-binding domain (short 6 kDa N-terminal domain) [Ref6813:White et al., 2023].

c_vaccine_name: BCG HSP65-MUC1 Fusion Protein Vaccine
c_description: A recombinant fusion protein vaccine consisting of BCG-derived heat shock protein 65 (HSP65) fused to two copies of the MUC1 variable-number tandem repeat (VNTR) peptide, with potential antineoplastic activity. The HSP65 component acts as a self-adjuvant, activating dendritic cells via TLR2/4 signaling and facilitating MHC class I cross-presentation of MUC1 epitopes to generate tumor-specific CTL responses. In MUC1-expressing B16 melanoma models, prophylactic vaccination reduced tumor weight (0.11g vs 2.01g control, p<0.001) and increased survival (53-73% vs 7%). Therapeutic vaccination in MUC1-expressing B16 melanoma reduced tumor weight (1.23-1.71g vs 5.31g, p<0.05) and increased survival (50-75% vs 0%, p<0.001). Similar results were obtained in MUC1-expressing EL4 lymphoma models. HSP65-MUC1 induced MUC1-specific CD8+IFN-γ+ T cells (0.56% vs 0.02%) in immunized mice and activated human DC with upregulation of CD40, CD80, CD83, CD86, and HLA-A2. MUC1 is a membrane-bound glycoprotein overexpressed in various epithelial cancers including breast, ovarian, lung, and colon carcinomas [Ref6804:Li et al., 2006].

c_vaccine_name: Allogeneic/Syngeneic DC-MC38/MUC1 Fusion Cell Vaccine
c_description: A fusion cell vaccine created by fusing murine MC38 adenocarcinoma cells expressing human MUC1 antigen with either allogeneic (BALB/c, H-2^d) or syngeneic (C57BL/6, H-2^b) dendritic cells using polyethylene glycol. The resulting heterokaryons express MHC class I and II molecules, costimulatory molecules (B7-1, B7-2, ICAM), and MUC1 tumor-associated antigen. Allogeneic fusion cells exhibit dual MHC haplotype expression (H-2^d/H-2^b). Vaccination reversed immunologic tolerance to MUC1 in MUC1 transgenic mice and induced potent CTL responses: syn-FC/MUC1 generated 50% lysis of MC38/MUC1 targets, 20% of MC38, and 1.46% MUC1-specific CD8⁺ T cells; allo-FC/MUC1 generated 32% lysis of MC38/MUC1, 25% of MC38, 0.71% MUC1-specific CD8⁺ T cells, with 2-3-fold higher T cell proliferation. Both vaccines provided complete protection against tumor challenge. In therapeutic studies, syn-FC/MUC1 completely eliminated pulmonary metastases (20/20 disease-free) and allo-FC/MUC1 was highly effective (17/20 disease-free), while PBS controls developed metastases (0/20). Demonstrates that allogeneic dendritic cells can be as effective as syngeneic dendritic cells for fusion vaccines, offering clinical advantages of unlimited healthy donor DC availability [Ref6814:Tanaka et al., 2001].

c_vaccine_name: Poly(HPMA)-MUC1(Tn)-TT P2-b-Poly(LMA) Conjugate Vaccine
c_description: A polymer-based nanoparticle vaccine consisting of tumor-associated MUC1 tandem-repeat glycopeptide with Tn antigen conjugated with tetanus toxoid T-helper cell epitope P2 on a poly(N-(2-hydroxypropyl)methacrylamide)-block-poly(lauryl methacrylate) [P(HPMA)-b-P(LMA)] carrier. The block copolymer structure self-assembles into micellar nanoparticles (~86 nm). Vaccination with this conjugate induced MHC-II-mediated IgG antibody responses (IgG1, IgG2a, IgG2b, IgG3) in mice. All antisera (6/6) recognized MCF-7 breast tumor cells, with the block copolymer formulation showing strongest tumor cell binding. The MUC1 glycopeptide contains immunodominant motifs (PDTRP and GSTAP) with Tn antigen at threonine-18. The P2 epitope provides universal T-helper cell support [Ref6815:Nuhn et al., 2013].

c_vaccine_name: α-Gal Epitope-Engineered MUC1-Expressing PANC1 Cell Vaccine
c_description: A whole tumor cell vaccine consisting of irradiated human pancreatic adenocarcinoma PANC1 cells genetically engineered to express α-Gal epitopes on surface glycoproteins. Upon vaccination, naturally occurring or induced anti-Gal antibodies bind to α-Gal epitopes on vaccine cells, forming immune complexes that enhance uptake by antigen-presenting cells via Fc receptors, leading to improved presentation of multiple tumor-associated antigens including MUC1, CD44, CD24, and ESA. Vaccination with pancreatic cancer cells (PANC1) elicited 8- to 16-fold increase in anti-MUC1 IgG (IgG1, IgG2b, IgG3 subclasses), expansion of MUC1-specific B cells (554 vs 320 per 10⁶ splenocytes; P < 0.0001) and IFN-γ-secreting T cells (1,238 vs 211 per 10⁶ splenocytes), and antibodies against CD44⁺CD24⁺ cancer stem cells. In α1,3GT knockout mice challenged with MUC1-expressing B16F10 melanoma cells, the vaccine demonstrated cross-protective immunity with significant tumor growth inhibition and prolonged survival (41.4 vs 21.1 days; P = 0.003), with 75-80% survival at 30 days compared to 20% for unmodified cell vaccine [Ref6816:Deguchi et al., 2010].
c_antigen: Multiple tumor-associated antigens (MUC1, CD44, CD24, ESA, others) [Ref6816:Deguchi et al., 2010]

c_vaccine_name: AuNP-MUC1-Tn Vaccine with (2S,3R)-3-hydroxynorvaline
c_description: A synthetic gold nanoparticle-conjugated glycopeptide vaccine containing MUC1 VNTR-derived Tn antigen (α-O-GalNAc) with (2S,3R)-3-hydroxynorvaline replacing threonine at the APDTRP immunodominant epitope, with potential antineoplastic activity. Vaccination with AuNP-MUC1-Tn with (2S,3R)-3-hydroxynorvaline elicits anti-MUC1 IgG antibody responses comparable to the natural threonine-containing variant (KD: 17 μM vs 19 μM for SM3 antibody binding). Immune responses are predominantly Th2-type with high IgG1 and low IgM/IgG2a/IgG2b/IgG3 levels. The unnatural amino acid enhances CH/π interactions with anti-MUC1 antibodies (4.2Å vs 4.7Å), and the SM3 antibody binding affinity correlates with immunogenic response in vivo, demonstrating structure-based vaccine design principles. PEGylated gold nanoparticles serve as both carrier and self-adjuvant. Antibodies elicited exhibit cross-reactivity with natural tumor-associated MUC1 and selectively target human breast cancer cells expressing aberrantly glycosylated MUC1 [Ref6817:Bermejo et al., 2024].

c_vaccine_name: pcDNA3.1-VNTR MUC1 DNA Vaccine
c_description: A plasmid DNA vaccine encoding a single tandem repeat unit (VNTR) of human tumor-associated mucin-1 (MUC1) antigen. The pcDNA3.1-VNTR construct contains one 20-amino acid repeat sequence with an optimized Kozak sequence and hMCP-1 (human monocyte chemoattractant protein-1) sequence engineered at the start codon region to enhance antigen expression and immune cell recruitment. Intramuscular vaccination induces potent MUC1-specific cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL) responses with 56.84±3.54% cytotoxicity at 80:1 effector-to-target ratio and 39.71±1.97% at 40:1 ratio, along with elevated anti-MUC1 antibody titers (P<0.05). In prophylactic studies, the vaccine significantly reduced tumor volumes (P<0.0001) and prolonged survival (P<0.05) in C57BL/6 mice challenged with MUC1-expressing pancreatic adenocarcinoma (panc02-MUC1). In therapeutic studies, vaccination initiated 4 days post-tumor inoculation significantly inhibited tumor growth (P<0.05) and extended survival time (P<0.05). The anti-tumor activity was completely MUC1-specific, with no protective or therapeutic effect observed against parental panc02 cells lacking MUC1 expression. MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein overexpressed in pancreatic, breast, and other epithelial cancers, represents a relevant target for cancer immunotherapy [Ref6818:Rong et al., 2009].

c_vaccine_name: (α-S-GalNAc)₃-TPE-P30-Tn-MUC1 Tripartite Glycopeptide Vaccine
c_description: A fully synthetic tripartite glycopeptide vaccine targeting the macrophage galactose-type lectin (MGL) on dendritic cells. The vaccine consists of three components: a trivalent α-S-GalNAc glycocluster on a tetraphenylethylene (TPE) scaffold for MGL binding and enhanced dendritic cell uptake, the P30 T helper epitope from tetanus toxoid, and a tumor-associated MUC1 tandem repeat glycopeptide bearing Tn antigens. The TPE glycocluster enhances binding to MGL by approximately tenfold (EC₅₀ 2.65 nM) compared to MUC1 glycopeptide alone and promotes fourfold increased receptor-mediated uptake by dendritic cells. Immunization with this construct induced over sevenfold higher titers of anti-Tn-MUC1 IgG antibodies compared to controls lacking the MGL-targeting glycocluster, with a mixed Th1/Th2 immune response (IgG1:IgG2b:IgG2c = 0.24:0.50:0.26). The antibodies produced recognize native MUC1-positive breast cancer cells and preferentially bind tumor-associated Tn antigens in the immunodominant PDTR region while showing reduced binding to core 2 and core 4 glycan structures typical of healthy cells. Administered with Freund's adjuvant in preclinical mouse studies [Ref6819:Gabba et al., 2023].

c_vaccine_name: Liposomal Pam₂-MUC1-Tn Vaccine with αGalCer
c_description: A fully synthetic liposomal vaccine containing a lipidated MUC1 glycopeptide antigen conjugated with two palmitoyl chains (Pam₂-MUC1-Tn) co-formulated with α-galactosylceramide (αGalCer) as an adjuvant, with potential antineoplastic activity. The vaccine consists of a MUC1 tandem repeat peptide sequence bearing the Tn carbohydrate antigen at the immunodominant PDTRP motif, with two palmitoyl lipid chains attached at the N-terminus. This amphiphilic antigen self-assembles into liposomes with αGalCer (NKT cell agonist), DSPC, and cholesterol. Vaccination with liposomal Pam₂-MUC1-Tn with αGalCer may stimulate humoral and cytotoxic immune responses against tumor cells expressing the MUC1 antigen. In preclinical mouse studies, the vaccine induced anti-MUC1 IgG antibody titers 190-fold higher than non-lipidated MUC1 and elicited mixed Th1/Th2 antibody responses with elevated IL-4 and IFN-γ cytokine levels. Antisera from vaccinated mice demonstrated complement-dependent cytotoxicity against MUC1-expressing MCF-7 breast cancer cells (34% survival rate). MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein, is overexpressed in an aberrant or deglycosylated form in approximately 80% of epithelial cancers including breast, prostate, and ovarian cancers [Ref6820:Du et al., 2019].

c_vaccine_name: Liposomal Diphtheria Toxoid₃₃₁₋₃₄₅ Epitope-MUC1 Glycopeptide + α-GalCer Vaccine
c_description: A fully synthetic liposomal conjugate vaccine containing tumor-associated MUC1 glycopeptide covalently conjugated with a diphtheria toxoid-derived T-helper epitope (DT₃₃₁₋₃₄₅, sequence: QSIALSSLMVAQAIP), adjuvanted with natural killer T (NKT) cell agonist α-galactosylceramide (αGalCer), and encapsulated in liposomes. Vaccination with DT-MUC1+αGalCer may stimulate both humoral and cellular immune responses against tumor cells expressing MUC1 antigen. The DT₃₃₁₋₃₄₅ T-helper epitope facilitates CD4+ T cell activation and promotes IgM to IgG class switching, while αGalCer activates NKT cells to enhance downstream immune responses, together synergistically enhancing MUC1-specific immunity, resulting in a 189-fold increase in anti-MUC1 IgG antibody titers compared to MUC1+αGalCer and 3-fold compared to DT-MUC1 alone, with CDC activity against MUC1-expressing tumor cells. The vaccine also induced potent cellular immune responses including CTL activity, and significant tumor growth inhibition in vivo. MUC1, a membrane-bound glycoprotein overexpressed and aberrantly glycosylated in various cancers including breast, colorectal, ovarian, lung, and prostate cancers, serves as the target antigen. The vaccine demonstrated a favorable safety profile with no significant adverse effects on major organs or liver and kidney function [Ref6825:Du et al., 2024].

c_vaccine_name: Pam₃CSK₄-MUC1-(Rha)₃ Liposomal Vaccine
c_description: A single molecular construct conjugate vaccine combining Pam₃CSK₄ lipopeptide, MUC1-VNTR tumor antigen, and tri-rhamnose targeting ligand, covalently linked and delivered via liposomes. The vaccine exploits natural human anti-rhamnose antibodies to target dendritic cells, stimulating both humoral and cellular immune responses against MUC1-expressing tumor cells. Vaccination enhanced anti-MUC1 antibody production and significantly increased antigen-specific CD4+ T cell proliferation (p < 0.001) in rhamnose-targeted groups. MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein hypo-glycosylated in various cancers, is overexpressed aberrantly in cancers such as breast, prostate, and ovary. No external adjuvant is required as Pam₃CSK₄ serves as a self-adjuvanting TLR-2 ligand built into the construct [Ref6826:Hossain et al., 2020].

c_vaccine_name: α-GalCer-AuNP-MUC1-Tn Vaccine
c_description: A conjugate vaccine containing MUC1-Tn tumor-associated glycopeptide antigen and α-galactosylceramide (α-GalCer) adjuvant, both covalently conjugated to gold nanoparticles (AuNPs) as a multivalent carrier, with potential antineoplastic activity. Vaccination with α-GalCer-AuNP-MUC1-Tn vaccine stimulates both humoral and CTL responses against MUC1-expressing tumor cells via iNKT cell activation through the CD1d pathway. MUC1 antigen, a transmembrane glycoprotein overexpressed in an aberrant glycosylated form in various cancers including breast, pancreas, lung and colon, is used as the tumor-associated antigen. The optimal 2:1 MUC1:α-GalCer formulation elicited high antibody titers (1:12,800), 54% complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC) against MCF-7 cells, a Th1-biased immune response (IgG2a/IgG1 >1), elevated IL-4/IFN-γ, enhanced DC maturation with increased IL-6/IL-12, and increased CD8+ T cell tumor infiltration, resulting in significant tumor growth inhibition in a B16-MUC1 melanoma model. In contrast, unconjugated MUC1+α-GalCer mixture showed minimal immune response due to NKT cell anergy [Ref6827:Liu et al., 2021].

c_vaccine_name: Qβ-MUC1-β-Tf Conjugate Vaccine
c_description: A synthetic glycopeptide-VLP conjugate vaccine containing a MUC1 glycopeptide bearing an unnatural β-linked Thomsen-Friedenreich (Tf) disaccharide [βGal-(1,3)-βGalNAc] covalently conjugated to bacteriophage Qβ virus-like particles (~220 glycopeptides per capsid), with potential antineoplastic activity. The unnatural β-glycosyl linkage provides significantly enhanced stability toward glycosidase degradation (no detectable cleavage after 24 hours versus near-complete cleavage of the natural α-linked MUC1-Tf glycopeptide within 1.75 hours). Vaccination with Qβ-MUC1-β-Tf conjugate with MPLA adjuvant successfully overcame MUC1 immune tolerance in human MUC1 transgenic mice, inducing high IgG antibody titers (mean 2,200,000 ELISA units, >1,000-fold over control) encompassing all major IgG subtypes with both Th1 and Th2 activation. The induced antibodies demonstrated complement-mediated cytotoxicity toward MUC1-expressing tumor cells equivalent to those induced by the natural MUC1-α-Tf vaccine. MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein overexpressed in aberrant or hypoglycosylated form in multiple cancers including breast, lung, pancreatic, colon, prostate, and ovarian cancers [Ref6828:Wu et al., 2021].

c_vaccine_name: CpG-Loaded MUC1-Tn Glycopeptide/P2 Tetanus Epitope Conjugate Cationic Nanohydrogel Vaccine
c_description: A self-adjuvanting conjugate vaccine containing tumor-associated MUC1-Tn glycopeptide (B-cell epitope) and P2 tetanus toxin-derived T-helper-cell epitope covalently conjugated onto CpG-loaded cationic nanohydrogel particles, with potential antitumor activity. Vaccination may stimulate humoral immune responses and T-cell proliferation against MUC1-expressing tumor cells without external adjuvants. In vivo studies in Balb/c mice (n=3/group) demonstrated rapid IgG antibody production after first boost with CpG-loaded vaccine versus five boosts required without CpG, both without CFA; no MUC1-specific antibodies detected without CpG after first boost; only CpG-loaded vaccine-induced antibodies showed binding to MUC1-expressing T47D human breast cancer cells with superior affinity; both vaccines induced T-helper-cell-mediated responses. CpG oligonucleotide complexed within the cationic nanohydrogel core activates intracellular TLR9, upregulating costimulatory markers CD40, CD80, and CD86 on dendritic cells to LPS-equivalent levels. MUC1 antigen, bearing truncated tumor-associated Tn carbohydrate antigen, is overexpressed in an aberrant form in epithelial cancers including breast cancer [Ref6829:Hartmann et al., 2015].

c_vaccine_name: MUC1 mRNA/CTLA-4 siRNA Co-Delivery Mannose-Modified NLE Vaccine
c_description: A dual-delivery vaccine employing mannose-modified nanolipid-exosome (NLE) nanoparticles to co-deliver modified MUC1 mRNA and CTLA-4 siRNA for triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) immunotherapy. The hybrid platform (90% exosomal membrane, 10% synthetic lipids) targets dendritic cells via mannose receptors, enabling in situ MUC1 antigen expression and simultaneous CTLA-4 checkpoint silencing. Vaccination with this platform may stimulate robust cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL) responses against MUC1-expressing tumor cells while preventing T cell exhaustion through CTLA-4 pathway inhibition. MUC1, a tumor-associated mucin and membrane-bound glycoprotein expressed by most glandular and ductal epithelial cells, is overexpressed and aberrantly glycosylated in TNBC and other epithelial cancers such as those of the breast, prostate, and ovary. In 4T1 mouse models, the combination therapy significantly enhanced tumor-infiltrating CD8+ T cells compared to vaccine or siRNA monotherapies (p < 0.01), increased MUC1-specific IFN-γ production (p < 0.01), and demonstrated robust antigen-specific cytotoxicity in vivo (p = 0.0015), with MUC1 protein expression confirmed in draining lymph nodes post-vaccination [Ref6790:Monfaredan et al., 2025].

c_vaccine_name: pVAX1-MUC1-6VNTR DNA Vaccine with C-terminal PDTRP Positioning
c_description: A plasmid DNA vaccine encoding six tandem repeats of the mucin 1 variable number tandem repeat (MUC1-VNTR) region with C-terminal PDTRP positioning for enhanced immunogenicity, constructed in the pVAX1 mammalian expression vector. Upon intramuscular administration, the plasmid DNA is taken up by host cells, which then express the MUC1-6VNTR protein and present it to the immune system, eliciting both humoral and cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL) responses against MUC1-positive tumor cells. The vaccine design features strategic positioning of the PDTRP pentapeptide sequence at the C-terminus of each VNTR unit, which confers stronger immunogenicity compared to N-terminal positioning. In preclinical studies, VNTR6 demonstrated the highest IFN-γ-producing CTL counts (105.2±8.7 vs 16.8±4.8 for empty vector; P<0.001) and strongest cytotoxicity against MUC1-positive Capan2 pancreatic cancer cells (41.25±3.34% vs 2.46±1.87% for control; P<0.001). The vaccine induced robust dendritic cell maturation with increased expression of CD80, CD86, and HLA-DR surface markers, elevated IL-12, IFN-γ, and IL-17 secretion, and superior tumor growth inhibition in mouse models compared to other VNTR variants (P<0.01). MUC1 antigen is a membrane-bound glycoprotein that is overexpressed in underglycosylated form in approximately 90% of pancreatic cancers and various other adenocarcinomas, making it a promising target for cancer immunotherapy [Ref6830:Gong et al., 2017].

c_vaccine_name: Rhamnose-Modified Liposomal Pam₃CysSK₄-MUC1-Tn Vaccine
c_description: A liposomal cancer vaccine containing a synthetic MUC1-Tn glycopeptide conjugated with Pam₃CysSK₄, with potential antineoplastic activity. Vaccination stimulates both CD4+ and CD8+ cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL) responses against tumor cells expressing the MUC1 antigen. In this vaccine, MUC1-Tn antigen is conjugated with Pam₃CysSK₄, a TLR2/1 agonist that serves as a self-adjuvant to enhance immune recognition and promote dendritic cell maturation. The vaccine is formulated in liposomes containing rhamnose-TEG-cholesterol, which recruits natural human anti-rhamnose antibodies to form immune complexes that enhance uptake by antigen-presenting cells through Fc receptor-mediated mechanisms. MUC1-Tn consists of a 20-amino-acid glycopeptide containing the Tn tumor-associated carbohydrate antigen (α-N-acetylgalactosamine). MUC1 antigen is a membrane-bound glycoprotein overexpressed in various cancers including breast, ovarian, and pancreatic cancers. In preclinical studies, administration of human anti-rhamnose antibodies (10 μg) one hour prior to vaccination (10 nmoles antigen, prime plus three boosts at 14-day intervals) enhanced CD4+ and CD8+ T cell priming, increased anti-MUC1-Tn antibody production, IFN-γ secretion, and cytotoxic activity against tumor cells. Both anti-rhamnose IgG and IgM isotypes were effective [Ref6831:Hossain et al., 2018].

c_vaccine_name: β-(1,3)-Glucan–MUC1 Conjugate Vaccine
c_description: A synthetic cancer vaccine candidate consisting of a MUC1 peptide antigen covalently conjugated to β-(1,3)-glucan polysaccharide via a PEG linker. The β-glucan component serves dual functions as both an antigen carrier and a self-adjuvant, eliminating the need for external adjuvants. The conjugate self-assembles into uniform nanoparticles (~162 nm) that facilitate antigen delivery. β-Glucan interacts with dectin-1 and other pattern recognition receptors (CR3, SIGNR1) on myeloid cells, activating both innate and adaptive immunity. MUC1 is a membrane-bound glycoprotein overexpressed on various cancer cells including breast, prostate, and ovarian cancers. In preclinical studies, vaccination elicited 13-fold ↑ anti-MUC1 IgG antibodies; IgM/IgG (predominantly IgG2b, IgG2b/IgG1 >1, Th1 dominance), cytotoxicity potential; dual immunity activation: IFN-γ ~4-fold↑, IL-6 ~4-fold↑ (p<0.01); antibodies reactive against MCF-7 breast cancer cells. Covalent conjugation was essential for immunogenicity; simple mixture of β-glucan and MUC1 peptide showed no significant immune response [Ref6832:Wang et al., 2018].

c_vaccine_name: DC Vaccine Transduced with Recombinant Ad5 with F35 Fiber Modification Encoding MUC1 cDNA (7VNTR) (rAd5F35-MUC1)
c_description: A dendritic cell-based vaccine using fiber-modified recombinant adenovirus serotype 5 with serotype 35 fiber chimera (rAd5F35) to transduce human monocyte-derived dendritic cells with full-length MUC1 containing 7 tandem repeats. Fiber modification enables efficient DC transduction (≥93%, ≥60% viability, 3 days). High-level MUC1 expression (≥500-1000 vp/cell) generates tumor-associated MUC1 glycoforms (Tn, T, sialyl-T; STn negative) on DC surface—the first demonstration of MUC1-transgenic DCs expressing cancer-associated glycoforms without glycosylation inhibitors. Transduced DCs maintain normal maturation with marked upregulation of HLA-DR, CD80, CD86, CD40, CD83; preserve naïve T-cell stimulation; and show 500-fold increased IL-12 production favorable for Th1/cytotoxic responses. Surface sialyl-T MUC1 does not shed or impair DC function, contrasting with recombinant ST-MUC1 studies. Tumor-associated MUC1 glycoforms may enhance antigen presentation through MHC class II-restricted presentation, direct T-cell recognition via MHC-unrestricted receptors, and B-cell activation. These glycoforms may bypass central tolerance as thymic medullary epithelial cells express fully glycosylated MUC1, not truncated forms. MUC1, a membrane-bound glycoprotein expressed by glandular and ductal epithelial cells, is overexpressed in aberrant or deglycosylated form in cancers including breast, pancreatic, and other carcinomas. This preclinical system provides basis for clinical dendritic cell vaccines targeting MUC1-expressing tumors [Ref6834:van Leeuwen et al., 2006].

c_vaccine_name: Nap-GᴰFᴰFᴰYᴰK-TSAPDT(Tn)RPAP Conjugate Vaccine
c_description: A self-adjuvanting peptide-based cancer vaccine consisting of the MUC1 tumor-associated glycopeptide antigen TSAPDT(α-GalNAc)RPAP covalently conjugated to the self-assembling peptide nanovector Nap-GᴰFᴰFᴰYᴰK. The nanovector, composed of naphthylacetic acid and D-amino acids, self-assembles into nanoparticles and serves as both carrier and adjuvant, eliminating the need for external adjuvants. Vaccination elicited robust humoral and cellular immune responses in BALB/c mice, with IgG antibody titers comparable to Complete Freund's Adjuvant (CFA). The vaccine induced Th1-skewed responses with IgG2a as the major antibody isotype, along with production of Th1 cytokines (IFN-γ, IL-2) and Th2 cytokines (IL-4, IL-5). Induced antibodies showed high binding affinity to MUC1-expressing MCF-7 breast cancer cells and mediated strong complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC). The covalently conjugated vaccine demonstrated superior immunogenicity compared to non-covalent mixtures of antigen and adjuvant. The MUC1 glycopeptide epitope (TSAPDT(α-GalNAc)RPAP) was validated on both synthetic peptide and native MUC1 on MCF-7 cells. The Tn antigen (α-GalNAc) at threonine represents a tumor-associated carbohydrate antigen characteristic of aberrantly glycosylated MUC1 on cancer cells [Ref5375:Liu et al., 2017].

c_vaccine_name: BSA-MUC1-TLR7a/Alum Binary Adjuvant Vaccine
c_description: A three-component conjugate vaccine consisting of MUC1 glycopeptide (13-mer: GVTSAPDTRPAPG) covalently conjugated to bovine serum albumin (BSA) carrier protein via a built-in TLR7 agonist, combined with aluminum hydroxide (Alum) adjuvant, with potential antineoplastic activity. This represents the first MUC1-targeted antitumor vaccine combining a self-adjuvanting protein conjugate with external adjuvant, creating a binary adjuvant system. Vaccination with BSA-MUC1-TLR7a/Alum stimulates potent humoral and cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL) responses against tumor cells expressing the MUC1 antigen. The vaccine elicits high anti-MUC1 IgG antibody titers (166,809) with Th1-biased immune responses (IgG2a/IgG1 ratio = 2.0). Serum antibodies effectively recognize and bind MUC1-positive MCF-7 breast cancer and B16-MUC1 melanoma cells and induce complement-dependent cytotoxicity (32% cell viability in MCF-7 cells). The vaccine generates MUC1 glycopeptide-specific CD8+ T-cell responses producing IFN-γ and TNF-α cytokines (2.6% IFN-γ⁺TNF-α⁺ CD8⁺ T cells) and high IFN-γ secretion (210 spots by ELISpot). In B16-MUC1 melanoma tumor challenge experiments, BSA-MUC1-TLR7a/Alum significantly inhibited tumor growth (mean tumor volume <500 mm³ vs >1,000 mm³ in controls) and prolonged survival time in mice. MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein expressed by most glandular and ductal epithelial cells, is overexpressed in an aberrant or deglycosylated form in various cancers such as those of the breast, ovary, and prostate [Ref6836:Zhou et al., 2022].

c_vaccine_name: MUC1-PD-L1-T helper epitope-IgG1 Fc Fusion Protein-Loaded DC Vaccine
c_description: A therapeutic dendritic cell vaccine loaded with a recombinant fusion protein (MUC1-Vax) containing human MUC1 extracellular domain, PD-L1 extracellular domain, T helper epitope sequence, and human IgG1 Fc fragment. The fusion protein is expressed in E. coli (ClearColi® BL21(DE3)), purified, and used to pulse syngeneic bone marrow-derived dendritic cells (BMDCs). The IgG1 Fc domain enhances antigen uptake by dendritic cells through Fcγ receptor-mediated endocytosis, improving cross-presentation to both MHC-I and MHC-II pathways. DCs are matured with LPS prior to administration. Vaccination elicits elevated anti-PD-L1 antibody production (significantly higher than PD-L1-only vaccine), increased CD4⁺ and CD8⁺ T cell activation with upregulated CD69 expression, and enhanced IFN-γ and IL-2 secretion, resulting in stronger CTL responses. In C57BL/6 mouse models bearing MUC1⁺ and PD-L1⁺ tumors (LLC-MUC1-PD-L1 and Panc02-MUC1-PD-L1), the vaccine significantly inhibited tumor growth, with complete tumor regression observed in some LLC-bearing mice, and prolonged survival compared to control groups. The dual-targeting MUC1-Vax vaccine demonstrated superior efficacy compared to PD-L1-only DC vaccine, providing a novel immunotherapy strategy for treating solid tumors with high MUC1 and PD-L1 expression [Ref6842:Pan et al., 2022].

c_vaccine_name: Site-Specifically Conjugated CRM197-MUC1 APDTRP Glycopeptide Vaccine with S-Glycosidic Tn and (4S)-4-Fluoro-L-Proline
c_description: A chemically defined glycoconjugate vaccine consisting of a synthetic non-natural MUC1 glycopeptide site-specifically conjugated to CRM197 carrier protein via disulfide re-bridging at Cys186-Cys201. The glycopeptide antigen contains the immunogenic APDTRP epitope with two non-natural modifications: (4S)-4-fluoro-L-proline and S-α-D-GalNAc (S-glycosidic Tn antigen), designed for enhanced immunogenicity and enzymatic resistance. Site-specific conjugation produces a homogeneous 1:1 conjugate, eliminating batch-to-batch variability while maintaining CRM197 structural integrity. Vaccination elicits a robust Th1-type immune response with predominantly IgG2a/IgG2b antibodies, elevated IL-2, IFN-γ, and TNF-α, and low IL-4, IL-10, and IL-13. Generated antibodies selectively recognize tumor-associated MUC1 on human cancer cells (T47D) and activate cytotoxic T-lymphocytes with ~20% tumor cell killing activity. In murine colon adenocarcinoma (MC38-MUC1) and pancreatic cancer (Panc02-MUC1) models, prophylactic vaccination reduced tumor volume by ~55% with complete prevention in 1/5 mice. Therapeutic vaccination achieved ~40-75% tumor reduction and 25-40% survival. Combined with anti-PD-1 checkpoint inhibitor, efficacy improved to ~70-84% tumor reduction, >20-80% survival, and one complete regression. MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein expressed by glandular and ductal epithelial cells, is overexpressed in aberrant or truncated glycosylated forms in various cancers including breast, colon, pancreatic, and ovarian cancers [Ref6843:Guerreiro et al., 2024].

c_vaccine_name: STn-MUC1-CRM197 Conjugate Vaccine with MPL/QS21
c_description: A synthetic glycopeptide vaccine containing a 21-amino acid MUC1 tandem repeat sequence modified with sialyl-Tn (STn) glycan, conjugated to CRM197 carrier protein via squaric acid chemistry, and formulated with MPL and QS21 adjuvants. Vaccination with STn-MUC1-CRM197 conjugate plus MPL+QS21 adjuvants elicited the highest anti-MUC1 IgG titers among tested formulations, with elevated levels across all IgG subtypes and a potent Th1-biased immune response characterized by elevated IgG2a. The vaccine demonstrated 43.5% complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC) against MCF-7 breast cancer cells, the strongest binding to MCF-7 cells among formulations tested, and enhanced antibody-dependent cellular phagocytosis (ADCP) activity. Glycosylated vaccines showed superior CDC activity (41.5-47.5%) compared to non-glycosylated vaccine (37.1%), demonstrating tumor-specific binding to human breast cancer tissues and the ability to break immune tolerance. The STn antigen (sialyl-Thomsen-nouveau) is a tumor-associated carbohydrate antigen found in nearly 90% of breast cancers but almost undetectable in normal tissue. MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein expressed by most glandular and ductal epithelial cells, is overexpressed in an aberrant or hypoglycosylated form in various epithelial cancers [Ref6844:Teng et al., 2025].

AuNP-Conjugated Fluoroproline-Modified S-Linked Tn-MUC1 Glycopeptide Vaccine
c_description: A synthetic cancer vaccine consisting of a chemically modified MUC1 glycopeptide conjugated to gold nanoparticles (AuNPs). The vaccine features an engineered MUC1-derived peptide with an artificial Tn antigen bearing an S-glycosidic linkage (oxygen-to-sulfur substitution) and a fluoroproline residue inserted in the peptide backbone. The glycopeptide is covalently attached to AuNPs via thiol-maleimide coupling. Vaccination in mice elicits high IgG1 antibody titers (Th2-type response) that cross-react with tumor-associated MUC1 (TA-MUC1) expressed on human breast cancer cells (MCF7, T47D), promote antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity (ADCC; 40% target cell lysis at 3:1 effector:target ratio), and specifically recognize cancer tissue in immunohistochemical assays of patient biopsies (n=5) with no binding to healthy tissue. Reducing the surface density of MUC1 antigen on AuNPs through co-loading with an ovalbumin-derived peptide maintains equivalent immunogenicity, demonstrating flexibility for future multicomponent vaccine design. MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein expressed on epithelial cells, is overexpressed with aberrant glycosylation characterized by short, truncated glycans in most epithelial cancers including breast, ovarian, lung, colorectal, prostate, pancreatic, and stomach cancers [Ref6845:Ghirardello et al., 2025].

c_vaccine_name: Thioether-Conjugated MUC1-diTn-P2(TT)-Pam₃CSK₄ Vaccine
c_description: A fully synthetic three-component cancer vaccine containing tumor-associated MUC1 tandem repeat glycopeptide with dual Tn antigens at threonine-9 and serine-15, tetanus toxoid P2 T-cell epitope (QYIKANSKFIGITE), and Pam₃CSK₄ lipopeptide (TLR2 agonist) linked via thioether conjugation. This self-adjuvanting vaccine achieves an end-point antibody titer of 100,000 in mice when administered in PBS buffer without external adjuvants, outperforming liposomal formulations. Vaccination elicits high levels of IgG1, IgG2a, and IgG3 antibodies that bind MCF-7 breast tumor cells and induce complement-dependent cytotoxicity (CDC), achieving 85% tumor cell killing. The MUC1 glycopeptide serves as the B-cell epitope, P2 peptide provides T-cell help, and Pam₃CSK₄ acts as a built-in adjuvant, eliminating the need for external adjuvant systems. MUC1 is overexpressed in various cancers including breast, ovarian, and colon carcinomas [Ref6846:Cai et al., 2013].

c_vaccine_name: QS-21-Derived Saponin–Poliovirus T-Helper Epitope–(Tn)MUC1 (Glyco)peptide Tricomponent Vaccine
c_description: A fully synthetic, tricomponent anticancer vaccine consisting of a QS-21-derived minimal saponin adjuvant covalently linked to a poliovirus-derived helper T-cell epitope (PV103-115, KLFAVWKITYKDT) and tumor-associated (Tn)MUC1 (glyco)peptide antigens. The vaccine exists in two variants: compound 6 (QA(PV)–MUC1) containing MUC1 peptide and compound 7 (QA(PV)–TnMUC1) containing TnMUC1 glycopeptide with Tn carbohydrate (GalNAc-α-O-Thr) on the SAPDTRPAP epitope. The three components are covalently conjugated via chemoselective ligation, creating a self-adjuvanting vaccine that spontaneously self-assembles into stable particulate aggregates in aqueous solution. Vaccination of C57BL/6 mice via subcutaneous injection (2-3 bi-weekly doses) with tricomponent vaccines induced significant anti-(Tn)MUC1 IgG antibodies (predominantly IgG1 and IgG2b subtypes) that recognized native TA-MUC1 on MCF7 cancer cells. Di-component constructs lacking the PV helper epitope or non-conjugated admixtures failed to elicit comparable responses, demonstrating that covalent linkage of all three components is required for immunogenicity. NMR studies revealed that tricomponent vaccines form stable, dilution-resistant nanostructures with surface-exposed (Tn)MUC1 antigens, while di-component constructs showed partial aggregate disruption upon dilution, correlating with reduced immunogenicity [Ref6847:Pifferi et al., 2023].

c_vaccine_name: T-glycosylated MUC1–YSYFPSV(TT)–Pam₃CysSer Vaccine
c_description: A tricomponent synthetic cancer vaccine combining per-T-glycosylated MUC1 VNTR peptide (20-mer: GVTSAPDTRPAPGSTAPPAH) as B-cell epitope, tetanus toxoid helper T-cell epitope (YSYFPSV), and Pam₃CysSer TLR2 agonist, covalently linked via ethylene glycol spacers. Immunization in C57BL/6 mice (20 μg) without external adjuvant elicited high IgG antibody titers (54,600), 21-fold higher than Tₙ-glycosylated variant. Antibodies demonstrated tumor selectivity, binding MCF7 breast cancer cells (22-48%) but not native MUC1 from normal tissue. Absence of IgM indicated establishment of immunological memory [Ref6848:Wilkinson et al., 2011].

c_vaccine_name: Mutant VEGF165b-MUC1 Fusion Protein Vaccine
c_description: A recombinant fusion protein vaccine consisting of plasmin-resistant VEGF165b mutant (mVEGF165b, containing A111P substitution) genetically fused via an AAY linker to a 24-amino acid MUC1 T-cell epitope peptide (STAPPAHGVTSPDTRPAPGSTAPP) derived from the Mucin1 VNTR region. The mVEGF165b component serves dual functions as both a protein carrier to enhance peptide stability and immunogenicity, and as an antigen to elicit anti-VEGF antibodies. Immunization induces high-titer anti-VEGF antibodies (1:1,400,000 titer) that reduce regulatory T cell (Treg) proportions, promote tumor blood vessel maturation, and enhance CD8+ T-cell tumor infiltration. The vaccine stimulates MUC1-specific cytotoxic T-lymphocyte responses, with CD8+ IFN-γ+ T cells increased 10-fold compared to control and 2-fold compared to individual components. In preventive BALB/c mouse models using Mucin1-expressing EMT-6 breast cancer cells, immunization extended median survival to 25 days versus 15 days in controls and demonstrated comparable efficacy to combined administration of separate mVEGF165b and MUC1 components. The MUC1 peptide targets aberrantly glycosylated Mucin1 overexpressed in more than 90% of breast and other cancers [Ref6849:Liang et al., 2024].

c_vaccine_name: 15Tn-MUC1 60-mer Glycopeptide-KLH Conjugate Vaccine
c_description: A glycopeptide conjugate vaccine containing a 60-mer MUC1 tandem repeat peptide with complete Tn glycosylation (15 GalNAcα1-O-Ser/Thr residues) conjugated to keyhole limpet hemocyanin (KLH), with potential antineoplastic activity. Vaccination with 15Tn-MUC1 60-mer glycopeptide-KLH conjugate may stimulate humoral and cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL) responses against tumor cells expressing cancer-specific Tn/STn-MUC1 glycoforms. The vaccine consists of three tandem repeats of the 20 amino acid MUC1 sequence (HGVTSAPDTRPAPGSTAPPA), with all five potential O-glycosylation sites per repeat occupied by Tn glycans. In this vaccine, the Tn-glycosylated MUC1 antigen is conjugated with KLH, an immunostimulant and a hapten carrier, to enhance immune recognition. MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein expressed by most glandular and ductal epithelial cells, is overexpressed in an aberrant or deglycosylated form in various cancers such as those of the breast, prostate, ovary, and pancreas [Ref6850:Tarp et al., 2007].

c_vaccine_name: Four-Component MUC1-diTn Conjugate Vaccine with Three T-Helper Epitopes
c_description: A fully synthetic four-component antitumor vaccine consisting of a tumor-associated MUC1 glycopeptide (22-mer) bearing two TN antigens (GalNAc-α-O) at threonine-11 and serine-17, covalently conjugated to three different bacterial T-helper cell epitopes via squaric acid linkage, with potential antineoplastic activity. The vaccine includes a 14-mer from Yersinia pestis, a 15-mer from Yersinia pestis, and a 20-mer from Mycobacterium tuberculosis as T-helper epitopes, separated by flexible triethylene glycol spacers. Vaccination elicits adaptive T-cell-mediated immune responses with predominantly IgG1 antibodies that recognize tumor-associated MUC1 on human breast cancer cells. In preclinical studies, the four-component vaccine induced antibody titers approximately 8-fold higher than vaccines containing a single T-helper epitope (~30,000 vs ~4,000 endpoint titers), with 71% binding to MUC1-expressing T47D breast cancer cells and formation of immunological memory. MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein expressed by most glandular and ductal epithelial cells, is overexpressed in an aberrant or deglycosylated form in various cancers such as those of the breast, prostate, pancreas, and ovary [Ref6851:Palitzsch et al., 2014].

c_vaccine_name: sp²-Iminosugar Tn Mimic MUC1 Glycopeptide-KLH Conjugate Vaccine
c_description: A synthetic glycopeptide-protein conjugate cancer vaccine containing a MUC1 epitope glycosylated with an unnatural sp²-iminosugar-based Tn antigen mimic, conjugated to keyhole limpet hemocyanin (KLH) carrier protein. The sp²-iminosugar modification replaces the natural O-glycosidic bond with a chemically and enzymatically stable sp²-hybridized pseudoamide linkage. Vaccination with sp²-iminosugar Tn mimic MUC1 glycopeptide-KLH conjugate vaccine elicits higher levels of specific anti-MUC1 IgG antibodies compared to the natural Tn antigen vaccine (P < 0.05), with predominantly IgG1 subtype (IgG1 > IgG2a). The elicited antibodies selectively recognize human breast cancer cells (MCF7, T47D) expressing tumor-associated MUC1, but not HEK293T cells lacking tumor-associated MUC1. A related glycopeptide containing the sp²-iminosugar Tn mimic exhibits 2-fold higher binding affinity to anti-MUC1 antibody scFv-SM3 (K_D = 1.60 ± 0.16 μM) compared to the natural Tn variant (K_D = 3.30 ± 0.84 μM). In this vaccine, the MUC1 glycopeptide is conjugated to KLH, an immunostimulant and hapten carrier, to enhance immune recognition. MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein expressed by most glandular and ductal epithelial cells, is overexpressed in an aberrant or deglycosylated form in various cancers such as those of the breast, prostate, and ovary [Ref6852:Bermejo et al., 2020].

c_vaccine_name: Qβ-MUC1-Tf/STn Vaccine
c_description: Two MUC1 glycopeptide vaccine variants were developed using the 9-amino acid protective epitope SAPDTRPAP glycosylated at threonine with either Thomsen-Friedenreich (Tf: βGal-(1,3)-αGalNAc) or Sialyl Thomsen-nouveau (STn: αNeu5Ac-(2,6)-αGalNAc) tumor-associated antigens, covalently conjugated to bacteriophage Qβ virus-like particles (~270 glycopeptides per particle) and administered with MPLA adjuvant via subcutaneous route on days 0, 14, and 28. In MUC1 transgenic mice modeling immune tolerance, both constructs elicited superior anti-MUC1 IgG titers (3.4M for STn; 2.5M for Tf ELISA units) with predominantly Th1-biased responses (IgG2b: 2.9M STn, 2.4M Tf; IgG2c: 1.7M STn, 0.49M Tf). Induced antibodies demonstrated PDTR region-selective binding, recognized multiple MUC1 glycoforms (Tn, Tf, cores 1-4) while sparing non-MUC1 glycoproteins, with Tf variant inducing broader glycoform recognition than Tn. Antibodies from both constructs bound MUC1-expressing melanoma (B16-MUC1) and breast cancer (MCF-7) cells while showing minimal binding to normal breast cells (MCF-10A), with Tf variant demonstrating superior B16-MUC1 binding (Tf>STn>Tn>unglycosylated) and highest complement-dependent cytotoxicity in vitro. Prophylactic vaccination with Qβ-MUC1-Tf significantly reduced lung metastatic tumor burden in a B16-MUC1 challenge model (p=0.008 vs PBS; p=0.003 vs Qβ), representing the first MUC1-Tf-based vaccine demonstrating in vivo tumor protection efficacy [Ref6853:Wu et al., 2019].

c_vaccine_name: CRM197-tetraMUC1-Tn Conjugate Vaccine
c_description: A semi-synthetic conjugate vaccine in which tumor-associated MUC1 (taMUC1) glycopeptide antigens displaying the Tn antigen (αGalNAc-O-Ser/Thr) are presented on synthetic cyclopeptide scaffolds in a tetravalent clustered configuration and covalently conjugated to the CRM197 carrier protein via squaramide linkages. When co-administered with the QS-21 adjuvant in C57BL/6 mice, the tetravalent conjugate elicited high levels of taMUC1-specific IgG antibodies (IgG1, IgG2b, IgG2c, and IgG3 isotypes), significantly activated CD4+ and CD8+ effector T cells (P<0.05-0.01), and demonstrated superior functional antibody binding to native taMUC1 expressed on MCF7 human breast cancer cells compared to monovalent conjugate or unconjugated scaffold formulations. The monovalent conjugate with QS-21 induced comparable IgG levels but weaker cancer cell binding. Administration without adjuvant resulted in reduced immunogenicity and CD8+ T-cell activation. The taMUC1 antigen is a 22-amino acid glycopeptide with Tn glycosylation at Thr18. MUC1 is a membrane-associated glycoprotein aberrantly overexpressed in most human epithelial tumors including breast (>90% of triple-negative cases), pancreatic, lung, ovarian, and prostate cancers, with malignant transformation leading to truncated glycans that expose the immunogenic Tn antigen epitope [Ref6854:Pifferi et al., 2026].

c_vaccine_name: PDTRP-MUC1-Calix[4,8]arene-Pam₃Cys-Ser Self-Adjuvant Vaccines (Tetravalent and Octavalent)
c_description: Synthetic multiepitope conjugate vaccines consisting of four (tetravalent, calix[4]arene scaffold) or eight (octavalent, calix[8]arene scaffold) copies of the PDTRP immunodominant B-cell epitope from the MUC1 core sequence, covalently conjugated to calixarene platforms with integrated Pam₃Cys-Ser (P3CS) TLR2 agonist as a self-adjuvant. The vaccines target tumor-associated MUC1, a membrane-bound glycoprotein overexpressed in aberrant or underglycosylated form in breast, ovarian, prostate, and other epithelial cancers. PDTRP represents the exposed naked peptide core in underglycosylated cancer-associated MUC1. Vaccination stimulates anti-MUC1 IgG antibody production through multivalent B-cell receptor cross-linking. The octavalent construct produces 2-fold higher anti-PDTRP IgG titers compared to the tetravalent construct (5120 vs 2560, p<0.05), attributed to greater conformational flexibility, extended epitope presentation, and superior electrostatic complementarity. Controls lacking PDTRP produced no anti-MUC1 IgG, confirming epitope essentiality. Induced antibodies recognize native MUC1 epitopes on MCF-7 human breast cancer cells, validating functional antibody production [Ref6855:Geraci et al., 2013, [Ref6856:Spadaro et al., 2020].

c_vaccine_name: hu(TA)MUC1 Glycopeptide (STn-T3/Tn-T16)–TTox Conjugate Vaccine
c_description: A synthetic glycopeptide vaccine containing a 22-amino acid human tumor-associated MUC1 (hu(TA)MUC1) tandem repeat peptide with sialyl-Tn (STn) antigen at threonine-3 and Tn antigen at threonine-16, conjugated to tetanus toxoid (TTox) via squaric acid chemistry. The vaccine targets aberrantly glycosylated MUC1 expressed on adenocarcinomas. Vaccination stimulates similar strong humoral immune responses in wild-type and huMUC1-transgenic mice with IgG1 and IgG2b antibodies (endpoint titers: 5×10⁵ and 5×10⁴ respectively); huMUC1-transgenic mice showed elevated IgM indicating reduced Th-mediated class switching due to partial tolerance. Antisera bound tumor-associated MUC1 on MCF-7 breast cancer cells (10.8–25.4% in wild-type; 4.58–18.2% in transgenic mice) with similar binding intensity, and significantly activated B cells, CD4⁺ T cells, and dendritic cells (p≤0.01–0.001). TTox provides T-helper cell epitopes sufficient to break immune tolerance in huMUC1-transgenic mice expressing MUC1 as a self-antigen, without inducing autoimmunity. MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein expressed by most glandular and ductal epithelial cells, is overexpressed in an aberrant or deglycosylated form in breast, pancreatic, prostate, stomach, colon, and ovarian cancers [Ref6857:Stergiou et al., 2017].
