c_vaccine_name: MUC1 (Glyco)peptide Vaccine: KLH/MAP-4/chimeric
c_description: A synthetic peptide vaccine targeting the MUC1 mucin core peptide sequence in three configurations with RIBI adjuvant: (1) KLH-conjugated peptides (SP1-7-KLH, SP1-14-KLH with Tn glycosylation), (2) MAP-4 dendritic clustered peptides (SP1-5 with full 20-amino-acid MUC1 tandem repeat; SP1-6 with CST-3 T-helper epitope), and (3) linear chimeric peptides (SP1-16 with tetanus toxin T-helper epitope). Tested in CAF1 mice bearing MUC1-transfected murine mammary adenocarcinoma (E3/410.4 cells), vaccination elicited configuration-dependent responses: SP1-5 induced poor IgG but strong DTH, achieving 52% tumor reduction prophylactically (p<0.03); SP1-7-KLH generated high IgG and DTH with 49-56% tumor reduction (p<0.002). Both significantly prolonged survival therapeutically (p<0.02), with cellular immunity (DTH) driving anti-tumor efficacy over antibody responses. Vaccine-induced IgG cross-reacted with E3 and human MCF-7 breast cancer cells. Vaccines target the immunodominant PDTRP epitope (B-cell epitope in mice; T-cell/CTL epitope in humans). MUC1 is a membrane-bound polymorphic epithelial mucin overexpressed in underglycosylated form in breast, pancreatic, and ovarian cancers, exposing cryptic peptide epitopes [Ref6859:Ding et al., 1993].

c_vaccine_name: MUC1 9mer (Glyco)peptide Vaccines (APG, SAP, APG-Tn, SAP-Tn)
c_description: A synthetic peptide vaccine containing short 9-amino acid MUC1-derived peptides (APG 9mer: APGSTAPPA; SAP 9mer: SAPDTRPAP) in both non-glycosylated and Tn-glycosylated forms (APG-Tn, SAP-Tn), adjuvanted with CpG 1826 oligonucleotide and Incomplete Freund's Adjuvant (IFA). The peptides are derived from the MUC1 tandem repeat (TR) region and correspond to H-2Db (APG) and H-2Kb (SAP) restricted epitopes. Vaccination generates increased CD4+ and CD8+ interferon-gamma producing T-cell responses with maximal avidity that demonstrate cross-recognition of both glycosylated and non-glycosylated MUC1 antigens, including tumor-associated MUC1, as well as intramolecular epitope spreading from the tandem repeat to cytoplasmic tail domains. The Tn glycosylation (αGalNAc O-linked to serine/threonine) mimics aberrant tumor-associated glycosylation patterns. In prophylactic settings, vaccination prior to B16.MUC1 tumor challenge provided 0% protection but induced immunoediting with decreased tumor MUC1 and MHC expression. Therapeutic vaccination continued post-tumor challenge achieved 30% complete tumor eradication (3/10 mice) with significant tumor growth delay (p=0.001). MUC1 is a membrane-bound glycoprotein overexpressed in an aberrant or underglycosylated form in approximately 75% of lethal human cancers including breast, pancreatic, and ovarian cancers [Ref6837:Lakshminarayanan et al., 2016].

c_vaccine_name: MUC1 22mer Peptide Vaccines (APG, SAP)
c_description: A synthetic peptide vaccine containing long 22-amino acid non-glycosylated MUC1-derived peptides (APG 22mer: APGSTAPPAHGVTSAPDTRPAP; SAP 22mer: SAPDTRPAPGSTAPPAHGVT), adjuvanted with CpG 1826 oligonucleotide and Incomplete Freund's Adjuvant (IFA). The peptides are derived from the MUC1 tandem repeat (TR) region and contain both H-2Kb and H-2Db restricted epitopes. Vaccination generates increased CD4+ and CD8+ interferon-gamma producing T-cell responses with high avidity that recognize the long peptides as well as some embedded 9mer epitopes, and demonstrates intramolecular epitope spreading from the tandem repeat to cytoplasmic tail domains. In prophylactic settings, vaccination prior to B16.MUC1 tumor challenge provided 0% protection, while Panc02.MUC1 challenge showed delayed tumor onset. Therapeutic vaccination with SAP 22mer continued post-tumor challenge achieved 40% complete tumor eradication (4/10 mice) with significant tumor growth delay (p=0.001), whereas APG 22mer was therapeutically ineffective. MUC1 is a membrane-bound glycoprotein overexpressed in an aberrant or underglycosylated form in approximately 75% of lethal human cancers including breast, pancreatic, and ovarian cancers [Ref6837:Lakshminarayanan et al., 2016].

c_vaccine_name: MUC1 Rotating Tumor Lysate Vaccines (C57mg, KCM, EL4, B16)
c_description: A whole tumor cell lysate vaccine composed of rotating lysates from four MUC1-expressing tumor cell lines (C57mg, KCM, EL4, B16) representing diverse tissue origins (mammary, pancreatic, lymphoma, melanoma), adjuvanted with CpG 1826 oligonucleotide and Incomplete Freund's Adjuvant (IFA). Lysates were prepared by freeze-thaw cycles and contain full-length, naturally glycosylated MUC1 with tumor-associated glycoforms. The rotating vaccination strategy (1st: C57mg; 2nd: KCM; 3rd: EL4; 4th: C57mg) generates the most diverse T-cell repertoire, with increased CD4+ and CD8+ interferon-gamma producing responses recognizing all 19 tested MUC1 peptides from both tandem repeat and non-tandem repeat regions, including preferential CD4+ recognition of glycosylated epitopes (19% for SAP Tn-9mer vs 9% for non-glycosylated SAP 9mer). In prophylactic settings, vaccination achieved 40-50% B16.MUC1 tumor rejections with significantly delayed tumor growth in non-rejecting mice (p<0.001), and prolonged survival in Panc02.MUC1 and MC38.MUC1 challenges. Adoptive transfer of lysate-primed T-cells after ex vivo activation achieved 100% cures in Winn assays. However, MUC1.Tg mice demonstrated incomplete immunological memory upon rechallenge, with tumor outgrowth showing decreased MUC1 and MHC expression. MUC1 is a membrane-bound glycoprotein overexpressed in an aberrant or underglycosylated form in approximately 75% of lethal human cancers including breast, pancreatic, and ovarian cancers [Ref6837:Lakshminarayanan et al., 2016].

c_vaccine_name: Autologous DC vaccine pulsed with Tn-MUC1 100-mer glycopeptide and KLH
c_description: An autologous dendritic cell vaccine loaded with Tn-MUC1 100-mer glycopeptide and keyhole limpet hemocyanin (KLH), with potential antineoplastic activity. Autologous monocyte-derived dendritic cells are loaded ex vivo with a 100-amino acid synthetic MUC1 glycopeptide bearing Tn carbohydrates (GalNAc-α-O-Ser/Thr) and KLH. The dendritic cells are matured with IL-1β, IL-6, TNF-α, and PGE2, then administered intradermally and intranodally. Vaccination may stimulate CD4+ and CD8+ T-cell responses against tumor cells expressing aberrantly glycosylated MUC1. The Tn-MUC1 glycopeptide contains five tandem repeats of the sequence GVTSAPDTRPAPGSTAPPAH from the human MUC1 VNTR region. Tumor-associated MUC1 is hypoglycosylated with truncated oligosaccharides such as Tn antigen (GalNAc-α-O-Ser/Thr), distinguishing it from normally glycosylated MUC1 on healthy epithelial cells. KLH serves as a positive control antigen to assess immune reactivity. In a phase I/II clinical trial in patients with non-metastatic castrate-resistant prostate cancer (n=16), the vaccine demonstrated safety and induced Tn-MUC1-specific CD4+ and/or CD8+ T-cell responses (predominantly IL-2+ and TNF-α+IL-2+) but no antibody responses in 5 of 7 evaluated patients, with KLH-specific responses in 6 of 7 patients. PSA doubling time significantly improved from 4.6 to 10.5 months in 11 of 16 patients (P=0.037). At 24 months, 3 of 16 patients remained progression-free. Preclinical studies in rhesus macaques demonstrated that Tn-rmMUC1-loaded DCs induced approximately 60% stronger IFN-γ+ T-cell responses compared to Tn-rmMUC1 with adjuvant [Ref6862:Scheid et al., 2016].

c_vaccine_name: Ser17-STn-MUC1-TTox Vaccine
c_description: A synthetic glycopeptide vaccine containing a 22-amino acid tumor-associated MUC1 tandem repeat sequence (PAHGVTSAPDTRPAPGSTAPPA) with a sialyl-TN (STn) glycan at serine 17, conjugated to tetanus toxoid (TTox) carrier protein, with potential antineoplastic activity. Vaccination with Ser17-STn-MUC1(22mer)-TTox vaccine stimulates humoral and cytotoxic T-lymphocyte (CTL) responses against tumor cells expressing aberrantly glycosylated MUC1. The vaccine elicited high titers of IgG1 antibodies (10,000-200,000 at half-maximal absorbance) in immunized BALB/c mice. The monoclonal antibody GGSK-1/30, derived from immunized mice, bound to 99% of MCF-7 breast cancer cells, 94% of T47D breast cancer cells, and 74% of PANC1 pancreatic cancer cells, while showing no binding to normal human mammary epithelial cells (HMEC). The antibody demonstrated exceptional diagnostic specificity, selectively staining tumor cells in human pancreatic adenocarcinoma and mucinous cystadenocarcinoma tissue sections obtained from patients, while not affecting normal pancreatic tissue. The STn glycan at Ser17 is essential for tumor cell recognition; non-glycosylated versions showed minimal tumor binding. MUC1 antigen, a membrane-bound glycoprotein expressed by most glandular and ductal epithelial cells, is overexpressed in an aberrant or deglycosylated form in various cancers such as those of the breast, pancreas, prostate, colon, and ovary [Ref6863:Palitzsch et al., 2016].

c_vaccine_name: ImMucin (MUC1-SP) Vaccine
c_description: A 21-mer synthetic long peptide vaccine (also known as VXL-100 or MUC1-SP-L) containing the entire MUC1 signal peptide domain, co-administered with human granulocyte-macrophage colony-stimulating factor (hGM-CSF). Unlike conventional MUC1 vaccines targeting the tandem repeat array (TRA) domain, ImMucin targets the signal peptide (SP) domain, which is free of soluble MUC1-related epitopes and features TAP-independent antigen presentation. The vaccine is formulated as a naked long peptide without traditional adjuvants or carrier systems; hGM-CSF is co-administered to enhance antigen presentation. In a Phase I/II trial of 15 MUC1-positive multiple myeloma patients with residual or progressive disease following autologous stem cell transplantation, vaccination induced mean 43.4-fold increase in MUC1-SP-specific IFN-γ-producing CD8+ T-cells, 3.5-fold increase in CD4+ T-cells, 94-fold increase in PBMC proliferation, and 68.6-fold increase in anti-ImMucin IgG antibodies in 10/15 patients (P<0.01), with antibody-dependent cell-mediated cytotoxicity achieving up to 32% specific lysis. Significant decrease in soluble MUC1 levels was observed in 9/10 patients (P<0.002). Stable disease or improvement persisting for 17.5-41.3 months was achieved in 11/15 patients; median progression-free survival was 17.5±3.9 months. Disease progression appeared associated with high PDL1 (CD274) bone marrow expression (PDL1+++ in all 3 progressive disease cases). Vaccination was well tolerated with only grade 1-2 adverse events. MUC1 is a membrane-bound glycoprotein overexpressed in an aberrant or deglycosylated form in various cancers including multiple myeloma, breast, prostate, and ovarian cancers [Ref6861:Carmon et al., 2015].

c_vaccine_name: SZU251 + MUC1 + Al vaccine
c_description: A three-component peptide vaccine containing a synthetic MUC1 peptide, a novel TLR7 agonist (SZU251), and an aluminum adjuvant (Alhydrogel). Vaccination stimulates both humoral and cellular immune responses against tumor cells expressing the MUC1 antigen. The MUC1 peptide includes a MUC1-derived epitope (SAPDTRPAP) and a murine MHC class II restricted T-helper epitope (KLFAVWKITYKDT). SZU251 acts as a TLR7-selective immunomodulator, promoting dendritic cell maturation (CD40, CD80, CD86 upregulation) and Th1-biased cytokine responses. The aluminum adjuvant enhances humoral immunity. In 4T1 triple-negative breast cancer mouse models, the vaccine elicited high MUC1-specific antibody titers (IgG/IgG2a: 2,048,000; IgM: 128,000), elevated CD8+ IFNγ+ T cells, tumor suppression, and extended survival (70-day observation). Serum antibodies demonstrated specific binding to MUC1-expressing 4T1 cells. The three-component formulation showed superior antitumor effects compared to two-component or single-component controls in both prophylactic and therapeutic schedules with good tolerability in BALB/c mice [Ref6866:Zhang et al., 2022].
